title: Compound duration strings ("1w 2d", "1h30m") with ordering, bare seconds and canonical formatting

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 1: w=604800, d=86400, h=3600, m=60, s=1 seconds per unit.
Rule 1: the result is the sum of all components.
Rule 1: unit letters are case-insensitive ("2H" equals "2h").
Rule 1: a component number is not limited by the next larger unit ("90m" -> 5400).
Rule 1: components are non-negative integers ("0h" -> 0).
parse_duration signature: returns the total number of seconds as an int.
Rule 2: components may be separated by any amount of whitespace or by nothing ("1w\t2d").
Rule 2: leading and trailing whitespace is ignored.
Rule 2: whitespace between a number and its unit is not allowed ("5 m" is invalid).
Rule 3: units in strictly decreasing size order are valid ("1d2h").
Rule 3: out-of-order units are invalid ("2h1d").
Rule 3: each unit at most once ("1h 1h" invalid); rule 1 case-insensitivity makes "1H1h" a repeat.
Rule 4: a string that is just an integer is seconds ("90" -> 90, " 0 " -> 0).
Rule 4: a number without a unit is not allowed inside a multi-component string ("1h 30").
Rule 5: empty or whitespace-only strings raise ValueError.
Rule 5: signs ("-5m", "+5m") raise ValueError.
Rule 5: decimals ("1.5h") raise ValueError.
Rule 5: unknown units ("5y", "5ms") raise ValueError.
Rule 5: any other characters such as separators or punctuation ("1h, 30m", "1h30m!", "h") raise ValueError.
Rule 5: a text argument that is not a str (90, None, b"1h") raises TypeError.
Rule 6: zero is "0s".
Rule 6: largest to smallest unit (w first), each component as large as possible, zero components omitted.
Rule 6: a negative value raises ValueError.
Rule 6: parse_duration(format_duration(n)) == n for every non-negative n.
retention.policy.expired must keep working and gains compound durations automatically.
